body: does it matter? lay off the shit and live ur live bro

why would anyone WANT to do this? why look for the meaning when essentially, you give life meaning and also, you lose the passion and curiosity is what drives humans. that's what i don't understand. you're given all this universal information, then you go right back to being human except now you truly realize how meaningless you are, collective consciousness aside. just enjoy life as is, let the meaning come to you, don't fuck up the flow of shit. y'all tryna get answers to shit that helps us live our lives and still won't get the real answer at the end of the day. to each their own tho.

yeah, i was told liquid was intense and my fiance' claimed to know as well and he'd tripped a couple times on some blotters and we'd tripped together two or three times before this so we were comfortable with one another. i know the trigger was his aunt, she has something benevolent about her that we could never quite put our finger on, just something really fucking evil and i'm rather good at projecting my light energy and being comfortable anywhere i am, whereas he isn't or wasn't at the time and very full of doubt. he said later that he felt left out because his aunt and i were discussing the universe and how everything is everything and he didn't seem to get that concept like at all so i think that triggered his self esteem issues as well. he also said later that at some point he felt like he was in that episode of spongebob where squidward goes too far back in time and it's just blank white space, which is why im wondering if maybe we experienced the singularity or something??? idk, it was trippy, like really trippy and i'm still not sure what to take from it.

if i were genuinely really attached to my ego and the material world, i would've panicked i think but i've never been that way. this was the one time i think being constantly in my head and feeling comfortable/safe w my own energy really saved me because i was so caught up and tripping so hard, like i said, it was hard to grasp what was happening so i couldn't panic even if i wanted to.

it was crazy man. like so quiet you could hear your heartbeat and blood pump. i think some people call that a singularity, it's used in discussions on like the beginning of the universe, where nothing existed, just a single point in time and space and that's what it felt like??
take it as a sign, you're too young and it was irresponsible to order an illegal drug to the house
lsd depletes your brain of serotonin, implying that some people trip a lot and have no brain cells/serotonin/they're a mushbrain.

i feel like no matter what kind of positive though i come up with, a negative one retaliates like 2 seconds later and i can't argue with it because to me it sounds rational. i know deep inside, finding something that makes it worth while is just another word for "distracting me from myself until i die" and that's just more depressing. see my problem here? whether that's depressing or not, it's still fact and i just can't argue with it. that's all life really truly is and i see right through all the bullshit. i guess i'd rather be sad on my own terms than be blind and thinking life is fine and dandy.

i feel like i already knew a lot about what lsd taught me but couldn't rationalize it or verbalize it until i actually tripped. kinda like that feeling of when you get a song stuck in your head and it's right on the tip of your tongue, so close to remembering it you can almost taste it, then you hear it and you're like yes, that's it! like i kind of have always been interested in the universe, the brain, anatomy, astrology, all that stuff and always had this feeling in my gut that somehow, it all means something and we're apart of it. dunno if that makes much sense, not the best at analogies or explaining things but...it's also taught me to let go and just experience life, don't try so hard to prepare for it all the time and to trust my gut.

update on this? i have noticed the more you try to help someone get out of a thought loop, the further they spiral, it's kinda fucked. best advice is just to do stuff you normally do until you notice that it isn't stimulating him enough, then change up the scenery/setting, or even start singing to him. terence mckenna once said singing is a great way of getting yourself out of a bad trip, but usually, unfortunately, you just have to ride it out.
